verdict.rationale: Channel3 documents an agentic search mode in which an LLM turns a natural-language request into filters and sub-searches. It also ships an official MCP server, so users can drive search and lookup in plain language from Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and similar clients, with no code or API key. Natural-language operation is evidenced mainly for search and lookup rather than the whole product, and hands-on reports show natural-language queries like "red high top sneakers under $40" returning irrelevant items and ignoring the price limit. missing for 10: evidence that natural-language commands cover operations beyond search (e.g., price-tracking subscriptions, account and billing actions), independent corroboration that agentic-mode interpretation is reliable, and documented examples of end-to-end natural-language workflows.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Toggle to agentic mode, and an LLM plans the search: it extracts deterministic filters, may split the request into OR/AND sub-searches
Connect Cursor, VS Code, Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, or OpenCode.
You can use it without writing any code, and without an API key.
